stem: Patrick is a 6-month-old infant with 2 days of coryzal symptoms and cough, now with wheeze, crackles, severe chest wall recession, grunting and hypoxaemia. Which one of the following is the most likely condition to account for his presentation?

options.text: Cardiac failure associated with febrile illness

explanation: This presentation is most consistent with bronchiolitis: a young infant with a viral prodrome, wheeze and crackles, marked work of breathing, and hypoxaemia. Asthma is less likely at 6 months, and the focal features of pneumonia are not described.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The item can be preserved because one existing option is clearly best supported by the clinical scenario. The question is made more specific by removing the surrounding table and repeated instructions, while keeping the source meaning intact.

optionExplanations.A: Cardiac failure can cause respiratory distress, but the preceding coryzal illness, wheeze/crackles, and age make bronchiolitis more likely.
optionExplanations.B: Pneumonitis is not the best fit for this viral prodrome with diffuse wheeze and crackles in a young infant.
optionExplanations.C: Asthma is uncommon as a first presentation in a 6-month-old infant and usually has a different clinical context.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: bronchiolitis classically affects infants, with coryzal symptoms, wheeze/crackles, tachypnoea, recession, and hypoxia.
optionExplanations.E: Sepsis can present with tachycardia and respiratory distress, but the respiratory viral history and chest findings are more typical of bronchiolitis.

Instructions

The following nine questions refer to Patrick’s clinical scenario.

Clinical scenario 1 - Patrick

Patrick, a six month old infant, is brought to the emergency department with wheezing and respiratory distress. On examination he has severe chest wall retractions, grunting and is pale. His vital signs are:

RR 80/min, HR 190/min, temperature 38.0’C, SaO2 80% in room air.

The accompanying table has the normal ranges indicated in the 2010 NSW Health Standard Paediatric Observation Chart, SPOC.

Patrick has wheeze and crackles throughout his chest. There is a history of having been snuffly with a cough for the last two days. The entire family has a cold.
